text: Fill in the missing terms from the section on nucleotide chemistry.
questions: Purines such as adenine and guanine have a fused double ring, whereas *pyrimidines:Which family of bases has the smaller, single ring?* have a single ring.
The sugar in DNA is *2′-deoxyribose/deoxyribose/2-deoxyribose/2'-deoxyribose*, which lacks the 2′-hydroxyl group found in ribose.
A base joined to a five-carbon sugar forms a *nucleoside*; adding phosphate converts it to a nucleotide.
The base attaches to carbon 1′ of the sugar through an *N-glycosidic/N glycosidic* bond.
Nucleotides in a polynucleotide chain are linked by 3′→5′ *phosphodiester* bonds, giving every strand a 5′ end and a 3′ end.

overallFeedback.feedback: These terms define the building blocks of all nucleic acids: the purine–pyrimidine distinction determines base-pairing rules, 2′-deoxyribose makes DNA chemically stable, the N-glycosidic bond and phosphodiester linkages give the polymer its directional backbone, and the thymine–uracil switch distinguishes the permanent archive from the short-lived working copy.
